newsitem.title: CHINA: S&P says to assign A-plus to Hutchison unit bond.
newsitem.headline: S&P says to assign A-plus to Hutchison unit bond.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Monday it expects to assign an A-plus long-term credit rating to Hutchison Whampoa Finance Ltd's upcoming US$1.0 billion 144a multitranche bond issue.
The issuer is a wholly owned financing subsidiary of Hong Kong-based Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, which is rated A-plus.
The bonds are expected to be issued in four tranches maturing in 2007, 2017, 2027 and 2037, and issue size, tranche size and coupon rate will be determined shortly, S&P said.
The rating reflects Hutchison's diversified earnings from service industries which are basic to Hong Kong's long-term prosperity, generating reliable cash flows and consistent returns, it said.
S&P said Hutchison enjoys strong market positions in its core businesses.

Its debt usage is moderate, with net debt-to-capital averaging about 18 percent in the past three years, although leverage is expected to rise in the next few years. Gross interest cover was about six times in the past three years.
Hutchison has ample substantial financial flexibility, which is derived from strong internal operating cash flow, large cash reserves, and sizable standby committed credit facilities, S&P said.
The outlook is stable and Hutchison is expected to maintain its strong financial profile in the next few years, it said.
